parsing_res_list.block_content: Reinforcement should have a minimum splice length and development length, Id, as required in TMS 402/ACI 530/ASCE 5, including the material reduction factor (i.e. φfactor). The reinforcing steel and masonry dynamic material strengths should be used to calculate the development length. All splices should be located in regions of low stress (i.e. no more than 75% of the maximum moment) and should be specified on the structural drawings to help ensure that splices are placed as intended. Additionally,splice lengths must be increased 30% if there are bars at each face of a cell (four per cell at splice locations) or if any of the bars are within 3 inches of each other. CMU walls with one layer of spliced reinforcement (i.e. at mid-thickness) should have at least a nominal thickness of 8 inches to help provide sufficient grout in the cells around spliced reinforcing steel. CMU walls with spliced reinforcement at each face should have at least a nominal thickness of 12 inches for the same reason. Non-contact splices are not allowed. Mechanical splices are allowed as permitted in Section 4-21.8.

Figure 6-10 (+) shows a reinforced CMU wall with spliced reinforcing bars. This figure shows two layers of reinforcement, but a single layer of reinforcement at midthickness is much more typical. Reinforced CMU walls are typically spliced at approximately 4 ft to 5ft height intervals in traditional low-lift wall construction, where the grout is placed by hand in the reinforced cells with a maximum pour height of 5 ft. The need to keep splices out of maximum moment regions may prevent the use of splices at the top of each grout pour and cause larger reinforcing steel lengths and associated block lift heights unless "A" or "H" blocks are used (see Figure 6-1 (+)), which is permitted.

Alternatively, high lift grout placement may be used according to the requirements of TMS 402/ACI 530/ASCE 5, which allows much longer lengths of unspliced reinforcement. The wall is built up to 24 ft high, or higher in some cases, clean-out cells are provided at the bottom of the wall, and grout is placed with a pump from the top of each reinforced cell. In the cases of both low-lift and high-lift construction techniques,inspection and quality assurance are essential to obtain composite action between the steel reinforcement and masonry as assumed for blast design.

required in TMS 402/ACI 530/ASCE 5, including the material reduction factor (i.e. φ
factor). The reinforcing steel and masonry dynamic material strengths should be used
to calculate the development length. All splices should be located in regions of low
stress (i.e. no more than 75% of the maximum moment) and should be specified on the
structural drawings to help ensure that splices are placed as intended. Additionally,
splice lengths must be increased 30% if there are bars at each face of a cell (four per
cell at splice locations) or if any of the bars are within 3 inches of each other. CMU
walls with one layer of spliced reinforcement (i.e. at mid-thickness) should have at least
a nominal thickness of 8 inches to help provide sufficient grout in the cells around
spliced reinforcing steel. CMU walls with spliced reinforcement at each face should
have at least a nominal thickness of 12 inches for the same reason. Non-contact splices
are not allowed. Mechanical splices are allowed as permitted in Section 4-21.8.
